summary: Specifies ways to use the Arcfour cipher in the Secure Shell protocol that reduce the weakness of the cipher's key-scheduling algorithm. It was a standards-track document, but it is now historic.

plainLanguage.summary: An old scrambler had a flaw in how it started up. This described a safer way to use it, but the scrambler is now outdated.

subtitle: Safer ways to use Arcfour encryption in SSH

tldr.problem: The Arcfour (RC4) cipher used in SSH has known weaknesses in its key-scheduling algorithm that can leak information about the key.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 4345 defines two new SSH cipher modes, arcfour128 and arcfour256, that discard the first 1536 bytes of keystream output to eliminate weak initial states that attackers can exploit.
tldr.outcome: These improved modes made Arcfour safer for SSH but are now historic as Arcfour itself has been deprecated in favor of stronger ciphers like AES.

today: RFC 4345 is Historic. Arcfour has been deprecated in SSH. Modern implementations use stronger ciphers like AES, which offer significantly better security properties.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content: Arcfour (also called RC4) is a fast stream cipher used in SSH to encrypt transmitted data. However, Arcfour has known problems: its key-scheduling algorithm can produce weak initial states that leak information about the key to attackers. Researchers found that discarding the first 1536 bytes of keystream prevents these attacks on the initial state.
sections.plainLanguage: Arcfour is fast but its first part is weak. Throwing away the first 1536 bytes of scrambled data makes it much harder to attack.

sections.title: Improved Modes
sections.content:
RFC 4345 specifies two new SSH cipher algorithms: arcfour128 uses Arcfour with a 128-bit key, and arcfour256 uses a 256-bit key. Both algorithms MUST discard the first 1536 bytes of keystream output. The first byte of data encryption uses the 1537th byte of keystream, not the first byte.

These modes remain fast and have small implementations, advantages over other encryption algorithms, but should only be used when speed and code size are critical and stronger alternatives are unavailable.
sections.plainLanguage: The two new modes are called arcfour128 and arcfour256. Each one throws away the weak part, then uses the rest normally. They are still fast but safer than before.

sections.title: Historic Status
sections.content: RFC 4345 is now Historic. Arcfour has been deprecated in SSH due to additional weaknesses discovered after publication. Modern SSH implementations use stronger ciphers like AES, which offer better security guarantees. These improved modes made Arcfour safer for their time but cannot be considered secure by modern standards.
sections.plainLanguage: Better scramblers were invented, so Arcfour (even the improved version) is no longer used.

references.text: Ylonen, T. and C. Lonvick, Ed., "The Secure Shell (SSH) Transport Layer Protocol", RFC 4253, January 2006.
